text:
Mikko Rantanen joined a short list on Tuesday. His second-period goal against Washington made him the fourth Finnish player to reach 800 NHL points, after Teemu Selanne, Jari Kurri and Saku Koivu, as Tom Gulitti of NHL.com noted. It was the middle game of a three-game goal streak.

The goals are the part to treat carefully. He has 9 on 5.1 expected, shooting 30% against 16% last season. A hat trick against Boston on Oct. 20 explains a chunk of it, and nobody keeps finishing at that rate.

The encouraging part is everything around the finishing. Dallas takes 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, 11 points better than without him, and he ranks 16th in the league in wins added by his goals. That's a brighter start than last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him 110th among forwards at 1.4 wins above replacement, a modest number for a player early in an eight-year deal.

Our projection has him around 31 goals. Watch the shot volume: 30 shots in 16 games is low for a winger his size, and when the percentages cool, more shots are how he keeps scoring.
headline: 800 points, and a hot stick to watch
